question: On the repository's prime-field instruments (ecbench ic.pipeline, counted GAE per sqrt(r), the AGENTS.md section 5a band at 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per native operation), what does the published naive Semaev index calculus cost: the small-abscissa factor base {P : x(P) in V}, V the N smallest abscissae carrying a point, decomposition by solving <S_(m+1)(x_1..x_m, x_R), F_V(x_1), ..., F_V(x_m)> with F_V = prod_(c in V)(x - c) in msolve over F_p, cold whole solve? How far is it from matched rho.negation, and where does it sit relative to the Table B incumbent on the same base and the same trial stream?

claims.text: Every reference-arm run recovers the planted logarithm, and on every trial point the msolve engine returns exactly the decompositions the exhaustive grid engine returns on the same system (relation-stream identity).

Distance remaining: the published reference arm (pub-m2-tuned) costs X times matched rho.negation at each measured size and band weight, with a 95% cluster-bootstrap interval; reported as distance, not as a pass/fail gate.

hypotheses.statement: At matched base size the published arm's group-operation count is close to the incumbent's (the same walked trial stream and the same hit law), while its msolve work per trial makes it far more expensive at w >= 0.1.
hypotheses.mechanism: Both arms see the same trial points on the same base; the incumbent pays a pair table once and a lookup per trial, the published arm pays one Groebner solve per trial whose cost grows like |V|^3.8 at m = 2 in the autoresearcher's msolve measurement.

positive.expected_detection: 1000/1000 planted points decompose with the planted pair among the solutions (any miss voids the arm); in addition, inside the main sessions, every trial index at which inc's exhaustive pair table found a decomposition on the shared walk must be a hit for pub-m2 (comparison C-hits)

null_population.description: trial points at which the exhaustive grid over V^m finds no decomposition; msolve must return no solution ([-1]) on every one (zero false positives), and pub-m2 and pub-m2-grid must emit byte-identical relation streams
null_population.generator: the shared walked trial stream of each pub-m2 execution, classified by the fp-grid engine on the same system
null_population.why_n: at least 1000 non-decomposing trial points per size (every size >= 12 bits yields more than this per execution); a zero false-positive count over 1000 bounds the rate below 0.3% (one-sided 95%)

power.note: targets per curve 48 at <= 18 bits, 24 at 20, 12 at 22, 8 at 24 (pub-m2 at 24 bits: 4, preflight-gated); 2 rounds. The 2026-10-29 tuning holdout resolved a 0.818 ratio to [0.773, 0.866] with 96 pairs; the predicted pub/rho and pub/inc effects at w >= 0.1 are one to three orders of magnitude, so the interval width is not the binding constraint. The three band weights are read jointly (ecbench band --ranks), not as separate tests.

placement.instance_type: FILL-AT-FREEZE (one x86 family for the whole study)

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design per panel and size as in sample_size.note; stop when every planned execution has a record

preflight gate: before the main sessions, run 4 targets x 1 round per size; if the measured pub-m2 per-solve time at a size exceeds 2 h, that size runs 4 targets x 1 round and its rows are labelled descriptive (no interval claimed)
any C-hits or C-grid mismatch, any msolve self-test failure, or any non-identical replay voids every pub-* record of that session
an execution that hits timeout_seconds is censored, recorded, and never re-run with a larger timeout

decision_rule.text: Admission (all must hold, else the arm is not established): every pub-* run verifies; C-hits and C-grid identical; msolve self-test passes at the session's p; ecbench verify --replay identical; C-aa-pub counted ratio exactly 1.000 and C-aa-rho exactly 1.000. Then C2 reports, per size and weight, sum S_pub-m2-tuned / sum S_rho-neg with its 95% cluster-bootstrap interval as the distance remaining. C3 reports ecbench band --ranks order of pub-m2 and inc: 'inc cheaper across band', 'pub cheaper across band', or 'unresolved' if the order flips between w = 0 and w = 1; it is context and is not an improvement verdict for either arm unless the owner rules that the table track may be ranked against the algebraic track. C5 reports f4_fp/msolve per size as win or loss only when outputs are equal on every system.
decision_rule.threshold: no pass/fail threshold on C-pub-rho (distance remaining); order statements only where they hold at w = 0, 0.1 and 1
decision_rule.statistic: ratio of summed S over matched (target, round) pairs (ecbench compare --weight W)
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: ratio of summed S per weight; fitted exponent difference

script.path: research/prime_ic_program_20261029/reference_arm/analysis.sh (to be written before freeze; thin shell over ecbench compare, band, bound fit)

inadmissible: changing N, sizes, targets, seeds, unit, band weights or accounting after seeing results
pricing msolve work by host wall time inside S, or leaving it out of the band
counting msolve process start-up or input parsing as algorithm work, or as zero work in the wall metric without saying so
reporting pub/inc as an improvement or regression of either arm while the cross-track ruling is open
quoting the w = 0 ratio alone for any arm with unpriced solver work
using a msolve build whose hash differs from the pinned one, or one that has not passed the self-test at the session's p
dropping censored executions from the means
invalidation_rules: a record whose msolve_sha256 differs from the pinned value
a replay that is not identical
a pub-* record from a session in which any C-hits or C-grid check failed

graphs: S per arm vs bits at w = 0, 0.1, 1 with intervals
